sentences.text: Macrogryphosaurus gondwanicus, meaning "big enigmatic lizard," is an elasmarian dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Patagonia, Argentina. It is noted for bony plates on its thorax and was identified as a large ornithopod.
A remarkable feature is its series of mineralized thoracic plates, also called intercostal plates. Its short torso, combined with a fused birdlike sternum, would have been rather stiff.
As a basal iguanodontian, it was likely a bipedal herbivore.
It is the largest known species of South American ornithopod excluding Hadrosauridae and the largest known elasmarian species.
Researchers consider the genus important because it is the largest known elasmarian and its complete remains inform on the group's anatomy.
An articulated, nearly complete skeleton was discovered in May 1999 at Mari Menuco Lake, Argentina, by the National University of Comahue. The fossil was found by a young boy named Rafael Moyano.
The species was formally described and named in 2007 by Jorge O. Calvo, Juan D. Porfiri, and Fernando E. Novas. The species name gondwanicus refers to the ancient supercontinent Gondwana.
The holotype specimen MUCPv-32 includes an essentially complete set of vertebrae, ribs, four thoracic plates, pectoral girdles, and a sternum.
The holotype MUCPv-321 is estimated at 6 meters long, and likely had not reached adult size due to unfused vertebrae. Dr. Stephen F. Poropat described the fossil preservation as "amazing."
Phylogenetic analysis links it to Talenkauen, leading Calvo and colleagues to propose the new clade Elasmaria for both genera.
It lived during the Coniacian age, approximately 89.8 to 85.7 million years ago.
